body.statement:
Let \(N\sim\operatorname{Bin}(n,\pi)\), where \(n\geq 1\), \(\pi\in(0,1)\), and let \(I_{\gamma}(N)\) be the two-sided equal-tailed Clopper--Pearson interval with total error level \(\gamma\in(0,1)\). Then
\[
 \Pr_{\pi}\{\pi\in I_{\gamma}(N)\}\geq 1-\gamma.
\]

source.verbatim_statement: The benefit of using an exact interval is obvious: one does not risk that the actual coverage falls below \(1-\alpha\).

attestation.note: Transcribed from the published author's manuscript, arXiv:1303.1288, Section 1; Section 2.1 identifies the exact interval as the two-sided Clopper--Pearson inversion.
